messages:
ash: Heads up — ran into a confusing state: saved query for route /v1/stream shows per-model breakdown that doesn't match current routing policy. It lists traffic on `redwood-legacy` even though rollout replaced it with `redwood-2025q1`.

jordana: can you paste the saved query payload? important to see whether it pinned an alias or canonical id.

ash: payload snip: `filters: { route: "/v1/stream", model: { pin: "redwood-legacy" }, timeframe: last_24h }` saved_at: 2025-03-22

pete: sounds like the pin is an alias that got repointed during the rollout. saved query load should resolve alias -> canonical_id at load time, but we probably cache the alias->id mapping at save time and never reconcile.

ash: behavior observed: after alias repoint, the console per-model card still shows the old model's metrics (throughput/cost). Users assume saved views reflect the route's live routing.

design_anna: UX note: we should avoid silently showing metrics from a different underlying model. At minimum show a callout: "Model alias has been repointed since this view was saved." Provide a restore-to-live button.

pete: proposal: change save semantics to store two fields: model_alias (string) AND model_canonical_id (optional). On load: if canonical_id present and matches current alias target -> normal. If mismatch -> show banner + mark used_snapshot=false but stale_mapping=true.

jordana: also add routing_policy_version to the saved view metadata so we can compare. If the routing policy changed (new version) then we know divergence is expected.

ash: telemetry wishlist: saved_view.open -> {alias_used: true/false, canonical_match: true/false, routing_policy_version_at_save, routing_policy_version_at_load, used_snapshot, live_fetch_latency_ms}.

pete: backend tasks: (1) extend saved_views table with model_canonical_id and routing_policy_version columns, (2) migration: for existing saved views, call model_catalog.resolve(alias) and populate canonical id where resolvable, (3) provide a reconciliation job that re-resolves aliases nightly and marks stale views for review.

infra-bot: migration note: Migration may touch ~18k saved views. Run in batches and set a concurrency limit. Watch schema migration rollbacks if the reconciliation job spikes DB.

jordana: UX copy options for banner: a) "Model alias `redwood-legacy` now points to `redwood-2025q1`. Metrics in this view reflect the model that was live when saved. [Compare live] [Use snapshot]" b) shorter: "Saved view may show metrics from an earlier model. Show live metrics?"

design_anna: prefer (a) — clearer. Add small tooltip explaining alias repointing and link to docs about routing policies.

pete: runtime behavior: prefer defaulting to live resolution (try resolve alias, then fetch live metrics with 700ms timeout). If resolution fails or fetch times out, show snapshot with banner. Don't fallback silently.

ash: another edge: saved queries used in scheduled reports expect deterministic numbers. We should offer an option "Always use snapshot for scheduled reports" in the save dialog.

jordana: yes and record report_policy: snapshot|live|hybrid in saved view metadata.

infra-bot: rollout plan: implement schema + migration behind feature flag. Deploy backend + reconciliation job, then UI toggle and banner. Canary on 5% for 24h, monitor saved_view.fallback_rate and saved_view.repoint_alerts.

pete: success metrics: fallback_rate < 0.5% post-migration, user-initiated restore-to-live click-through > 10% when banner shown (indicates discoverability).

design_anna: I'll produce a quick mock for the banner + restore flow. Will post Figma link in this thread when ready.

ash: ok volunteers? I'll write the RFC covering edge cases (scheduled reports, cross-route aggregations). pete + jordana review backend + telemetry. design_anna will take the mock and copy.

jordaNA: small typo: it's jordana ;)

ash: thanks — will post RFC draft tomorrow. :rocket:
